definition: In digital lexicography, natural language processing, and digital humanities, a lexical resource is a language resource consisting of data regarding the lexemes of the lexicon of one or more languages e.g., in the form of a database..
details: In digital lexicography, natural language processing, and digital humanities, a lexical resource is a language resource consisting of data regarding the lexemes of the lexicon of one or more languages e.g., in the form of a database.

explainer.lead: A lexical resource is structured data about the lexemes of one or more languages, typically held in a database. It matters as the reference material underlying digital lexicography, NLP and digital humanities work.

tiers.eli5: It is a well-organised word bank: not just a list of words, but information about them that software can look up.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers draw on lexical resources for dictionaries, word senses and word properties in NLP pipelines. A pitfall is coverage: a resource built for one language or domain may leave gaps elsewhere.
tiers.paperLevel: Defined in digital lexicography, NLP and digital humanities as a language resource consisting of data regarding the lexemes of the lexicon of one or more languages, for example in database form. The definition does not fix a schema.

explainer.example: A word-sense database listing each lexeme with its meanings and relations is a lexical resource queried by a disambiguation tool.
